thread:
ava: thinking out loud — proposal for a new runtime config primitive: "sticky overrides". idea: allow an override to be bound to a tenant/session with TTL and automatic leak protection so experiments don't persist accidentally. want quick reactions before i draft API + console UI.

sam: +1 conceptually. curious about how we define affinity: session vs tenant vs request. also how this interacts with batching/caching.

ava: affinity options: "session", "tenant", "user". session = stick to a connection/session id for TTL; tenant = all traffic from that org; user = single user id. caching: sticky should be applied after route resolution but before prefix caching so TTL is honored.

marta: product note — console needs to show active sticky overrides and an easy "revoke" action. also a clear TTL indicator. non-technical PMs will expect to see who created it and why.

jin: operational concerns: if many sticky overrides accumulate it could blow out our routing table memory. propose a global cap per-tenant (e.g., 500 active stickies) and eviction policy LRU or sampled TTL bump.

ava: agree on cap. thinking default cap 200, warn at 150. UI should surface cap usage. eviction should prefer oldest and those flagged as ephemeral.

sam: telemetry: we should emit a distinct metric: `sticky.override.created` with labels affinity, creator, TTL, source (api/console). also `sticky.override.evicted` and `sticky.override.leak_detected`. sample payloads for audit logs?

ava: yep. audit events need override id, creator, scope, reason, created_ts, revoked_ts. also link to trace id when applied to a request.

lex: security checklist — sticky overrides must be optional for private deployments. and enforce RBAC: only certain roles can create tenant-scoped stickies. also KMS access is irrelevant but include proof in audit.

marta: UX question: should the console allow "sticky preview" where you can pick a small cohort and visually inspect routing over a time window? could be helpful before flipping.

jin: technically we can do shadow stickies for preview: apply override in shadow mode (no effect on routing) and collect diffs for 10m. ops-bot can run a replay job.

config-bot: dry-run results for shadow sticky (id: stky-2026-09-12-001) — 10m window, 0.6% requests would hit different model variant, mean latency +2ms, cost delta +0.8%.

sam: API sketch (very rough):
```http
POST /v1/runtime/overrides
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "scope": "tenant",        // tenant | session | user
  "selector": {"tenant_id": "org-123"},
  "config_delta": {"route.default.model": "ggml-3-small"},
  "sticky": true,
  "ttl_seconds": 3600,
  "max_stick_percent": 5,   // leak protection: max % of tenant to be sticky
  "eviction_policy": "lru|oldest",
  "mode": "active|shadow"
}
```

ava: nice. `max_stick_percent` helps prevent runaway experiments. also add `telemetry_sample_rate` to control metrics volume.

marta: console: show a quick simulation estimator: estimate affected QPS % and cost delta (based on recent 1h profile). allow an approval step for >1% impact.

jin: rollout safety: implement server-side guard that rejects creation if (current_sticky_coverage + estimated_impact) > tenant_cap_percent. fallback: accept in shadow mode only.

sam: edge cases: what if a sticky targets a route that later gets deleted? need stable references (route ids) and graceful fallback. record original route id in audit and mark sticky as "orphaned" if mismatch — auto-expire after short TTL.

ava: good call. also TTL extension policy: owner can extend but cannot exceed a company-wide max (e.g., 24h) unless ops approves.

lex: add RBAC flag `require_2fa_for_tenant_sticky` for high-risk tenants.

ops-bot: noted. queued a canary enforcement job to enforce tenant-wide cap for `org-123` next deploy window.

marta: small UX nit: label stickies in console with icons: shadow = purple dot, active = green, orphaned = ⚠️. also include creator initials.

sam: what about analytics overhead? if many stickies we might sample 1% traces but still need counters for eviction/leak events. default telemetry_sample_rate = 0.01.

jin: implement fast-path check in router: lookup sticky map by (tenant, session) — if hit, attach override id to ctx and increment local counter; else fallback. keep sticky map sharded and TTL-evictable.

ava: next steps: i'll draft RFC with API shape + console mocks + telemetry contract. can someone volunteer to review the infra bits (sharding/eviction)?

jin: i'll take infra review.

sam: i'll own telemetry schema and event names.

marta: i'll prototype console list + revoke flow.

ava: great — thanks team. leaving this open for a couple days for comments. if no blockers i'll file RFC Thursday. :thumbsup:

config-bot: automated note — created draft RFC issue: #rfc/sticky-overrides-2026-09 (link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rfcs/1234).
